chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about butter (samen) in which a dead animal falls, so he said: 'If it is solid, throw away what is around it and eat the remainder.' I said: 'What about oil?' He said: 'Sprinkle it (use) it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming butter or oil if a dead animal falls into it?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istihlak* (dilution) and the distinction between solid and liquid contaminants. While solid butter requires discarding the affected portion, liquid oil is deemed sufficiently mixed to remain permissible for use, reflecting the practical application of purity laws in daily life. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease (*rukhas*) in matters of food consumption when contamination is not overwhelming.
